measures.name: Addressable market
measures.definition: Size of the opportunity the technology opens, for anyone.

anchors.mid: 5: material category, ~$1B-scale, or credible path to it.
anchors.high: 8–10: reshapes a multi-billion category or creates one.

measures.required_evidence: At least one analyst or primary market figure WITH its scope and date recorded. One TAM figure is thin support — say so.
measures.open_question: The $100M and $1B marks for a low and a high score: to confirm with Tata.

measures.name: Growth
measures.definition: The rate the space is expanding — capital, players, deployments — not its current size.

anchors.low: 0–2: flat or contracting interest; funding and entrants declining.
anchors.mid: 5: steady growth; new entrants each year, funding trending up.
anchors.high: 8–10: inflecting — funding rounds accelerating, hyperscaler entry, standard-body urgency.

measures.required_evidence: Dated series or repeated events across the evidence window (funding, launches, adoptions), not a single enthusiastic article.

measures.name: Use-case breadth
measures.definition: How many distinct TCL-relevant problems the technology addresses.

anchors.mid: 5: a family of related uses within one fabric.
anchors.high: 8–10: broad horizontal utility across several fabrics or industries TCL serves.

measures.required_evidence: Distinct named use cases, each with at least one piece of evidence; hypothetical uses do not count.

measures.name: Fabric fit
measures.definition: How squarely the technology sits inside one of TCL's fabrics — assessed per fabric.

anchors.low: 0–2: touches the fabric only by analogy; no plausible TCL service embeds it.
anchors.mid: 5: adjacent — fits the fabric's domain but would extend, not deepen, current offerings.
anchors.high: 8–10: core — directly upgrades or threatens services this fabric sells today.

measures.required_evidence: Technical descriptions concrete enough to map onto the fabric's services; at least one piece of evidence naming a use in this fabric's domain.

measures.name: Portfolio adjacency
measures.definition: How close the technology is to what TCL already operates — assets, platforms, skills.

anchors.low: 0–2: nothing TCL runs today is reusable toward it.
anchors.mid: 5: TCL's assets help (network, PoPs, enterprise relationships) but the core capability is new.
anchors.high: 8–10: TCL could credibly deliver it by extending an existing platform or asset.

measures.required_evidence: What the technology needs to operate (infrastructure, data, distribution), mappable against the TCL portfolio.
measures.open_question: Depends on the TCL portfolio description, pending stakeholder interviews.

measures.name: Right to play
measures.definition: Whether TCL would be a credible provider in the eyes of buyers — beyond mere capability.

anchors.low: 0–2: buyers would not shortlist a carrier for this; incumbents own the trust.
anchors.mid: 5: TCL could earn a seat via partnerships or an anchor customer.
anchors.high: 8–10: carrier-grade trust, global reach or regulatory standing is exactly why buyers would pick TCL.

measures.required_evidence: Who buys it, from whom today, and what the buying criteria are.

measures.name: Maturity (TRL)
measures.definition: Technology readiness, expressed on TCL's TRL-style scale.

anchors.mid: 5: working prototypes, early field trials, pre-standard (TRL 4–6).
anchors.high: 8–10: productised, deployed at scale, standards ratified (TRL 7–9).

measures.required_evidence: Dated evidence of demonstrations, trials, deployments or ratified standards — a vendor claim alone does not raise TRL.

measures.name: Commercial adoption
measures.definition: Real buying behaviour, distinct from technical maturity.

anchors.mid: 5: early adopters and lighthouse deals; revenue exists, references are few.
anchors.high: 8–10: repeatable purchasing across segments; named production customers at scale.

measures.required_evidence: Named deployments, revenue disclosures, procurement or operator announcements — repeated coverage of the SAME deal counts once.

measures.name: Deliverability
measures.definition: How hard it would be to stand this up and run it at carrier grade — the risk axis. High score means EASY to deliver.

anchors.low: 0–2: severe blockers — unresolved physics/scale problems, hostile regulation, single-vendor lock.
anchors.mid: 5: hard but chartable — skills or ecosystem gaps that money and time close.
anchors.high: 8–10: deliverable with known engineering; mature supply chain and operational patterns.

measures.required_evidence: What deployments actually required (skills, capex, timelines, dependencies); regulatory posture where relevant.

measures.name: Disruption threat
measures.definition: If TCL does nothing, how badly does this hurt existing revenue? The only defence-oriented measure.

anchors.low: 0–2: no plausible impact on any current revenue line.
anchors.mid: 5: erodes one line over years; substitution is possible but sticky.
anchors.high: 8–10: direct substitution for a major line, already being marketed at TCL's customers.

measures.required_evidence: Evidence of substitution actually happening or being sold — competitor positioning, customer pilots replacing incumbent services.
measures.open_question: Depends on the TCL portfolio description, pending stakeholder interviews.

measures.name: Serviceable capture
measures.definition: The slice of the opportunity TCL could realistically win.

anchors.low: 0–2: TCL's channels and assets reach almost none of it.
anchors.mid: 5: a definable segment (existing enterprise base, specific geographies) is winnable.
anchors.high: 8–10: TCL's position makes it a natural top-3 provider for a large share.

measures.required_evidence: Market shape by segment/geography against TCL's footprint. Depends on addressable-market being scorable; inherit its thinness.

measures.name: Capability gap
measures.definition: What TCL lacks to pursue this, and how expensive the gap is to close. High score means the gap is SMALL.

anchors.low: 0–2: the gap is the business itself — talent, IP and platforms all absent.
anchors.mid: 5: buildable or buyable within normal investment horizons.
anchors.high: 8–10: TCL substantially has what it needs today.

measures.required_evidence: What delivering requires versus what the portfolio shows TCL operates; hiring or acquisition signals where present.
measures.open_question: Depends on the TCL portfolio description, pending stakeholder interviews.
